- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce peak overshoots by 5–10% to avoid overreacting to bullish sentiment.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay downward correction by 1–2 periods to account for sentiment lag.
- Model tends to overestimate upward momentum in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) — apply a 3–5% downward bias to short-term forecasts when sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.2), model often misreads trend direction — use a 2-period moving average of sentiment to smooth forecast adjustments.
- Forecast errors cluster near 15–30 day horizons — apply a 3–5% upward bias to mid-term forecasts when sentiment is trending upward, to account for mean reversion in carbon markets.
- If forecast peaks exceed true outcome by >10% and sentiment is positive, assume sentiment is overblown — reduce peak by 10–15% and shift downward slope by 1–2 periods.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below forecast), model often fails to adjust — apply a 5–10% downward correction to next 3–5 periods if sentiment is weak or neutral.
